hero.title: Kayal means backwater. It's where our food comes from.

origin.heading: The lagoon and the table
origin.intro: In Kerala, the kayal is the slow water between the rice paddies and the sea — home of the kettuvallam houseboats, the toddy shops on stilts, and the kind of cooking that never needed a recipe book. Fish straight off the line into the clay pot. Tapioca and beef on a rainy afternoon. Lunch tied up in a banana leaf.
origin.aboutParagraph: Kayal has a long history of serving innovative and creative Indian cuisine. We try to reflect the essence of true India and an authentic approach to Indian cuisine from across the majestic sub-continent. We take great pride in serving a high-quality and authentic South Indian food menu to our customers.
origin.chefBio: Our kitchen is led by a chef with around seventeen years of cooking in Kerala before bringing the village table to Sydney.

kizhiPorotta.heading: The Kizhi Porotta
kizhiPorotta.story: Kizhi Porotta is cooked porotta stuffed with fried curry meat — usually beef or chicken — wrapped in banana leaf and tied into a bundle. The bundle is steamed, then grilled on a hot skillet with coconut oil, adding the aroma of banana leaf and coconut oil to the filling.

chattiChoru.heading: The Chatti Choru
chattiChoru.story: Chatti Choru is a combination plate of rice, a variety of curries, and non-veg items, all served in a wide earthen pot.
chattiChoru.bestSellerLine: It's our best seller for a reason: the clay holds the heat, the heat holds the flavour, and the flavour holds the memory.

miniMart.heading: Take Kerala home
miniMart.text: Our grocery corner stocks the essentials — matta rice, spice mixes, pickles and the things a Kerala pantry can't do without. Ask us on your way out.
